visual_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1 more accurately and clearly depicts the 30° velocity decomposition with correctly placed horizontal and vertical component vectors and matching formulas, while Lesson 2’s tiny projectile diagram is conceptually relevant but its component arrows/labels are much less positionally clear and the vertical axis arrow can be misleading as the vertical velocity component.

interactivity.rationale: Lesson 2 has a clearly wired, functional fill-in gate after act_introduction with a real prompt, accepted answers, hint, and remediation path, whereas Lesson 1 has no available gate specs or plan and therefore no evidence of any functioning checkpoint.

narration_quality.rationale: Lesson 2 provides clear, natural narration with spoken math phrasing and no raw LaTeX or garbling, while Lesson 1 has no available narration transcript at all and therefore cannot demonstrate any audio clarity or pacing quality.

sync.rationale: Lesson 2 provides timed visual cues that are mostly aligned with the narration's references, while Lesson 1 has no transcript or timing data at all, making it impossible to verify any synchronization.

concept_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 2 correctly decomposes the velocity, uses vertical motion to get flight time and horizontal constant velocity/range with the correct 141.4 m result, while Lesson 1 has no available transcript or lesson content to verify accuracy or learner support.

polish.rationale: Lesson 1 has larger, more legible text and a cleaner, brighter mid-lesson layout with consistent colors, while Lesson 2’s mid-lesson diagram is tiny, dim, pushed into the lower-left with excessive empty space and low-contrast labels despite its cleaner dark title screen.

aggregator.explanation: Lesson 2 is the clear overall winner: four high-confidence agents favored it, including interactivity (0.99), synchronization (0.98), concept accuracy (0.96), and narration quality (0.95). These were core instructional dimensions, and Lesson 1 lacked available evidence for narration, timing, interactivity, and verified conceptual development. Lesson 1 was preferred only on visual accuracy (0.77) and polish (0.78), mainly due to clearer component-vector placement and more legible layout. However, those lower-confidence advantages are outweighed by Lesson 2’s strong functional checkpoint, accurate physics explanation, aligned timing, and clear narration.
